- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast 2–5 days after peak by 2–5% to align with mean reversion.
- In high-sentiment periods, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply “mean reversion buffer”: if price deviates >5% from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward average.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates early in the period when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; add 0.5–1.5% to first 5–7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by reducing amplitude of swings by 10–20%.
